result.title: Regularizing Treatment Leakage for LLM-based Uplift Estimation
result.summary: Uplift modeling estimates the conditional average treatment effect (CATE) and supports industrial decisions such as promotional pricing. When large language models (LLMs) encode product text, treatment-revealing content can introduce shortcuts that do not transfer to deployment. We propose \emph{LLM-based Uplift Leakage Regularization} (\textsc{LULR}), which uses a CLUB-based penalty on the causal head's trainable shared representation while keeping the LLM encoder frozen. Controlled proxy experiments show a positive ranking-score interaction and higher scores than the tested weight-decay configuration; treatment-dependent evaluation limits their interpretation to exploratory model behavior. Structured-only comparisons provide reference performance, without establishing a general advantage over tree-based estimators. On a million-record industrial pricing RCT, \textsc{LULR} improves offline $\text{lift@}0.3$ in $4/5$ seeds, although the difference is not statistically significant and estimated policy values are near-tied. A separate one-week online A/B experiment records $5.45\%$ higher sales volume and $1.91\%$ higher GMV than the control arm. These aggregate results provide short-term business evidence for the complete deployed pricing policy; they do not isolate the regularizer's contribution.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 LLM 编码商品文本的 uplift/CATE 估计中「treatment 泄漏」造成的捷径问题，提出 LULR：冻结 LLM 编码器，对因果头共享的可训练表示施加 CLUB 互信息惩罚，并用代理实验、百万级工业定价 RCT 与一周在线 A/B 评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 以 CLUB 惩罚抑制共享表示中与干扰变量（treatment）相关的可预测信息，可供核查作为约束 latent 推理状态保留哪些证据、剔除虚假线索的表示正则手段；但论文非多模态、无推理期状态生成，迁移到 LVR 属推测。
